target_customer: Social media users who want more civil discussion of current events through video
problem: Text based online debate was uncivil. Greo required users to respond with video of up to 60 seconds so faces and voices were attached to opinions.
business_model: Consumer social app, monetization not stated

founders.name: Brandon Hill
founders.background_notes: Blavity (June 29, 2017) says all three co-founders are Stanford graduates. He later co-founded Vori, a grocery technology company.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile video recording, upload and threading app is standard consumer engineering for a small team in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on a critical mass of users in video conversations, but features were easy to copy and the video only rule was a product choice, not a barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Greo. The YC page lists it inactive.

market_need_then: The founders pitched a need for more civil online conversation. No dated source on measured demand was found.

branding.domain_note: Used greo.com, an exact .com, which currently returns only the single word greo.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about discovering, creating and exchanging meaningful ideas to awaken a more just world, per the YC page

branding.brand_signature: Video only conversation with faces required, as described by Blavity
branding.community_and_virality: Covered in the Black founder press by Blavity and Rolling Out in 2017 and 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: Some founder focused press attention, but no evidence of a widely recognized consumer brand or community.

outcome_analysis: Greo was a three person Stanford founded team that joined YC in Summer 2017 with a video only conversation app and raised a reported $120K seed. No shutdown notice, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause of inactivity is not public and no failure factors are assigned. The CEO went on to build Vori, a grocery operating system, which suggests the team moved on from the product.
notes: greo.com returned only the word greo when fetched, so the site is effectively dead. The $120K seed rests on CB Insights alone, which also says two rounds totaling about $120K, so a second round is unidentified. CB Insights lists Knit as a competitor but describes it as a market research firm, a different business from group video calling, and gives no date near the batch, so it is not listed. Competitor list is empty because no source dated near the Summer 2017 batch named a rival. The Rolling Out interview returned 403 and was not opened. The move to Vori as an explanation for the end is an inference from a search snippet.
